purpose: Few-shot example findings, one per heuristic id, used as voice/shape references when the model writes findings. NOT templates — the model should pattern-match style and specificity, not copy structure verbatim.
usage_notes: Examples are intentionally terse. Designers scan; long descriptions get skipped. Target: title ≤8 words, description ≤30 words, suggestion ≤20 words. ~50 words per finding total. Variety across recipes, e-commerce, dashboards, signup, settings, messaging, editors prevents context fixation.

schema.title: Headline of the finding (≤8 words, ≤80 chars)
schema.description: 1–2 short sentences anchored to a specific screen and element (≤30 words)
schema.suggestion: 1 concrete fix — what to add and where (≤20 words)

loading.skeleton-vs-spinner.title: No loading state for the dashboard
loading.skeleton-vs-spinner.description: Screen 1 mocks the populated dashboard but not the loading frame. Users see a blank page until data arrives.
loading.skeleton-vs-spinner.suggestion: Add a skeleton: greyed rectangles for each chart and KPI card, matching the grid.

loading.optimistic-rollback.title: Like button has no designed failure state
loading.optimistic-rollback.description: Screen 2 shows the heart filled when liked, but no frame for when the server fails to register it.
loading.optimistic-rollback.suggestion: Add a failure frame: heart un-fills, toast 'Couldn't save your like' with a Retry link.

loading.long-operation-progress.title: Export jumps from button to completed report
loading.long-operation-progress.description: Screen 3 shows 'Generate Report' then the finished file. Nothing in between for a 10+ second operation.
loading.long-operation-progress.suggestion: Add an in-progress frame: progress bar, brief status, and a cancel button.

loading.background-refresh-indicator.title: Live feed has no refresh indicator
loading.background-refresh-indicator.description: Screen 1's activity feed gives no signal that data is refreshing, or that newer items have arrived.
loading.background-refresh-indicator.suggestion: Consider an 'Updating…' label in the header and a 'View 3 new posts' pill on new content.

loading.action-acknowledgment.title: Submit button has no in-flight state
loading.action-acknowledgment.description: Screen 2's 'Submit' is only mocked in its default state. What it looks like while submitting is undefined.
loading.action-acknowledgment.suggestion: Add an in-flight state: disabled, inline spinner, label 'Submitting…'. Keep width fixed.

empty.first-time-vs-cleared.title: Inbox has only one empty-state variant
empty.first-time-vs-cleared.description: Screen 1 shows a single 'Your inbox is empty' state. First-time users and users who've cleared everything see the same thing.
empty.first-time-vs-cleared.suggestion: Design two: first-time ('Your messages will appear here') and cleared ('Inbox empty — view archived').

empty.filtered-no-results.title: No empty state for zero filter results
empty.filtered-no-results.description: Screen 2's filtered grid has no frame for when filters return zero — it falls back to the generic empty.
empty.filtered-no-results.suggestion: Add 'No products match these filters' with a 'Clear filters' button and a suggestion to remove the most restrictive.

empty.search-no-results.title: Search has no 'no results' state
empty.search-no-results.description: Screen 3 only mocks search with results. No frame for empty results, no echo of the search term.
empty.search-no-results.suggestion: Add a no-results state quoting the term: 'No results for "<term>".' Include 'Did you mean' and 'Browse all'.

empty.permission-restricted.title: Restricted-access state looks identical to empty
empty.permission-restricted.description: Screen 1's Team Projects shows 'No projects here' for users without workspace access — same view as a truly empty workspace.
empty.permission-restricted.suggestion: Design a distinct restricted state: 'You don't have access' + 'Request access' button.

error.recovery-path-present.title: Payment-error state has no recovery action
error.recovery-path-present.description: Screen 4 shows 'Payment could not be processed' with no buttons or links. Nowhere to go from here.
error.recovery-path-present.suggestion: Add 'Try Again', 'Use a Different Card', and 'Contact Support' buttons below the error.

error.scope-matches-cause.title: All errors use the same full-width banner
error.scope-matches-cause.description: Screen 2 shows field errors and form-level errors both as full-width red banners. Scope of the problem isn't visually distinct.
error.scope-matches-cause.suggestion: Inline errors under the offending field; reserve the banner for whole-form problems.

error.differentiate-failure-modes.title: One generic error frame for every failure
error.differentiate-failure-modes.description: Screen 5 uses one 'Something went wrong' frame for offline, server-down, and validation — all needing different copy and recovery.
error.differentiate-failure-modes.suggestion: Design three frames: offline ('Changes will sync'), server-down ('Servers unreachable'), validation ('Correct highlighted fields').

error.preserve-user-input.title: Error state shows the signup form empty
error.preserve-user-input.description: Screen 3's error-state mockup has empty fields with the banner above. Signals that resetting on error is fine.
error.preserve-user-input.suggestion: Re-render the mockup with the user's input visible — error message above, fields preserved.

auth.session-expired-mid-action.title: No state for session expiry during editing
auth.session-expired-mid-action.description: Screen 2's editor supports long sessions, but no design for what happens when the session expires mid-draft.
auth.session-expired-mid-action.suggestion: Add an in-context re-auth modal and a return-state showing the draft intact after sign-in.

auth.protected-screen-logged-out.title: Protected /settings has no logged-out state
auth.protected-screen-logged-out.description: Screen 1 shows /settings populated, but no frame for a logged-out user landing there directly.
auth.protected-screen-logged-out.suggestion: Add a logged-out state: 'Sign in to manage your settings' + sign-in CTA, then return to /settings.

auth.unallowed-action-visible.title: Viewer-role version of admin actions isn't mocked
auth.unallowed-action-visible.description: Screen 3 shows Edit, Delete, and Settings fully active. The PRD's 'viewer' role isn't mocked for this screen.
auth.unallowed-action-visible.suggestion: Decide hide vs. disable. If disabled, gray out with a tooltip. If hidden, mock the viewer's variant.

auth.reauth-for-sensitive-action.title: No re-auth step before account deletion
auth.reauth-for-sensitive-action.description: Screen 5's account deletion goes button → 'Are you sure?' → done. No re-auth challenge despite the consequence.
auth.reauth-for-sensitive-action.suggestion: Consider a re-auth modal — type password to confirm — before the deletion is committed.

validation.server-rejection-after-client.title: No state for 'email already in use'
validation.server-rejection-after-client.description: Screen 1's signup handles invalid email format, but not the case where the email is valid yet already taken.
validation.server-rejection-after-client.suggestion: Add a post-submit state: 'This email is already in use. Sign in instead?' under the field.

validation.format-hints-pre-error.title: Password field has no format hints
validation.format-hints-pre-error.description: Screen 2's password field shows only a label and placeholder. Requirements appear only after a failed submit.
validation.format-hints-pre-error.suggestion: Consider a live requirements list below the field: '✓ 8 characters / ✗ One number / ✗ One special'.

validation.async-availability.title: Username uniqueness check isn't designed
validation.async-availability.description: Screen 1's username field has only its default state — no checking, available, or taken-with-suggestion variants.
validation.async-availability.suggestion: Add three states: spinner while checking, '✓ Available', '✗ Taken — try "<suggestion>"'.

validation.required-vs-optional-signal.title: Required and optional fields look identical
validation.required-vs-optional-signal.description: Screen 3's contact form has nine fields with no asterisks, 'Optional' labels, or helper text marking required ones.
validation.required-vs-optional-signal.suggestion: Pick a convention — red asterisks + 'Required' legend, or '(optional)' tags — and apply uniformly.

connectivity.offline-mode.title: Chat app has no offline state
connectivity.offline-mode.description: Screen 2's messaging assumes connectivity. No offline banner, no queued-message indicator, no fallback for send.
connectivity.offline-mode.suggestion: Add a banner ('You're offline — messages will send when you reconnect') and a queued-clock on pending messages.

connectivity.slow-network.title: Image-heavy feed has no slow-network state
connectivity.slow-network.description: Screen 1's feed assumes images load quickly. No low-res placeholder, no 'taking longer than usual' messaging.
connectivity.slow-network.suggestion: Consider a low-res blur that resolves as the image loads, plus a delayed-load message after ~8s.

connectivity.request-timeout.title: Loading state has no timeout fallback
connectivity.request-timeout.description: Screen 3's loading state shows a spinner indefinitely. If the request hangs, no retry, no cancel, no acknowledgment.
connectivity.request-timeout.suggestion: After ~15s, replace the spinner with 'This is taking longer than usual' and [Keep waiting] [Retry] [Cancel].

connectivity.retry-ux.title: Failed-load state has no retry button
connectivity.retry-ux.description: Screen 2's 'Couldn't load your feed' state has no retry. The only option is a full page refresh.
connectivity.retry-ux.suggestion: Add a [Retry] button where the feed would appear. Retry should preserve filters and pagination.

data.long-text-overflow.title: Card titles only mocked at short lengths
data.long-text-overflow.description: Every product card on Screen 1 has a tidy 2–4-word title. No example shows truncation, wrap, or expand behavior.
data.long-text-overflow.suggestion: Include one card with a 60+ character title. Specify truncation (e.g. 2 lines + ellipsis, full on hover).

data.null-or-missing-fields.title: Profile only mocked with full data
data.null-or-missing-fields.description: Screen 4 shows a profile with bio, location, website, and avatar all set. No variant for missing optional fields.
data.null-or-missing-fields.suggestion: Mock a sparse profile: empty bio (or 'Add a bio' for owner), default avatar, missing fields handled cleanly.

data.large-numbers.title: View counts only mocked at small numbers
data.large-numbers.description: All post cards on Screen 2 show counts under 1,000. No mock at viral scale (50K, 1M, 10M+).
data.large-numbers.suggestion: Add one card at '2.5M views' and specify the formatting threshold ('1.2K', '3.4M') so raw integers don't ship.

data.i18n-text-expansion.title: Design only proofed in English
data.i18n-text-expansion.description: PRD mentions international markets, but every screen uses short English labels. German runs 30–40% longer.
data.i18n-text-expansion.suggestion: Consider a German variant of key screens to verify the layout holds. Flag directional icons for RTL.

concurrency.stale-data-edit.title: No conflict state for collaborative editing
concurrency.stale-data-edit.description: Screen 1's shared editor supports multiple users, but no design for when User A saves after User B's update.
concurrency.stale-data-edit.suggestion: Add a conflict modal: 'Updated by Jamie 3 min ago' + [View their changes] [Overwrite] [Discard mine].

concurrency.action-while-loading.title: Bulk actions active while list still loading
concurrency.action-while-loading.description: Screen 2's 'Delete selected' looks active before the file list finishes loading. Users could act on partial state.
concurrency.action-while-loading.suggestion: Add a disabled toolbar state while loading, with a 'Loading files…' tooltip.

recovery.undo-destructive.title: Email deletion is final once confirmed
recovery.undo-destructive.description: Screen 3's delete-email flow goes through a confirmation modal but ends there. No undo state once confirmed.
recovery.undo-destructive.suggestion: Consider an undo toast — 'Email moved to Trash. [Undo]' for ~5s — alongside or instead of the modal.

recovery.confirm-irreversible.title: Account deletion uses generic 'Are you sure?'
recovery.confirm-irreversible.description: Screen 6 protects account deletion with the same modal used for canceling a draft. Friction is out of proportion.
recovery.confirm-irreversible.suggestion: Design a proportional confirm: type the account email — delete stays disabled until it matches.

recovery.autosave-indicator.title: Editor has no save-state indicator
recovery.autosave-indicator.description: Screen 1's editor shows content but no signal of whether changes have been saved. Users can't tell if auto-save is working.
recovery.autosave-indicator.suggestion: Add three states near the title: 'Saved', 'Saving…' (spinner), 'Unsaved changes' (warning).

a11y.error-not-color-only.title: Field errors rely only on red borders
a11y.error-not-color-only.description: Invalid fields on Screen 2's signup show only a red border — no icon, no helper text. Invisible to red-green color blindness.
a11y.error-not-color-only.suggestion: Add a warning icon and helper text ('Please enter a valid email'). Red border becomes one of three signals.

a11y.touch-target-size.title: Mobile breakpoint uses desktop icon sizes
a11y.touch-target-size.description: Screen 3's mobile variant keeps icon buttons at 16px — sized for mouse, not touch. Adjacent buttons sit tightly.
a11y.touch-target-size.suggestion: Resize icon buttons to ≥44×44px on mobile, with ≥8px separation between adjacent targets.

counts.singular-vs-plural.title: Selection bar only mocked for plural counts
counts.singular-vs-plural.description: Screen 1's file picker shows '5 files selected'. The singular case isn't mocked — would render as '1 files'.
counts.singular-vs-plural.suggestion: Mock '1 file selected' and '2 files selected'. Optionally include '0 selected' as a disabled state.

counts.too-many.title: Notification badge only mocked at small counts
counts.too-many.description: Screen 2's bell shows '3 unread'. No variant for high counts (200, 2000+) — engineering picks how to render them.
counts.too-many.suggestion: Add a '99+' variant for counts over 99. Specify the cutoff so engineering doesn't guess.

counts.one-item-affordance.title: Carousel only mocked with multiple items
counts.one-item-affordance.description: Screen 4's 'Related products' carousel shows five items. No variant for one item — arrows would point to nothing.
counts.one-item-affordance.suggestion: Mock a single-item variant: hide arrows, optionally reflow to a centered card without carousel chrome.

actions.success-confirmation.title: Order flow ends at 'Place Order'
actions.success-confirmation.description: Screens 2–4 end with the 'Place Order' button. No screen shows what happens after success — order number, summary, next steps.
actions.success-confirmation.suggestion: Add a confirmation screen: order number, item summary, delivery estimate, 'Continue shopping' or 'Track order'.

actions.disabled-primary.title: Primary action only mocked in active state
actions.disabled-primary.description: Screen 2's 'Continue' button appears only active. The disabled case — and what enables it — isn't shown.
actions.disabled-primary.suggestion: Mock the disabled state: grayed-out with tooltip 'Complete required fields to continue'. Visually distinct from active.

actions.selected-active.title: Sidebar nav has no active-state design
actions.selected-active.description: Screen 1's left sidebar shows nav items in a single style. The active/selected item isn't designed.
actions.selected-active.suggestion: Mock the active state: distinct background, left-edge accent bar, bolder label. Clearly different from hover.

hierarchy.subject-identity.title: Recipe screen doesn't show the dish name
hierarchy.subject-identity.description: Screen 1 shows a photo, ingredient grid, and cooking steps — but the dish name doesn't appear anywhere. Users don't know what they're making.
hierarchy.subject-identity.suggestion: Is the name handled elsewhere in the flow? If not, place it as a prominent heading above the image.

hierarchy.primary-action-dominance.title: Three buttons compete for primary attention
hierarchy.primary-action-dominance.description: Screen 1's action bar shows 'Cook', 'Save', and 'Watch' as equally-weighted pills. No signal of which is primary.
hierarchy.primary-action-dominance.suggestion: Pick one as primary — solid fill, brand color — and let the other two recede into outline styling.

hierarchy.above-the-fold-value.title: Primary content sits below the fold
hierarchy.above-the-fold-value.description: Above the fold on Screen 1: nav, hero photo, QR code. The dish name, metadata, and 'Cook' button require scrolling.
hierarchy.above-the-fold-value.suggestion: Tighten the above-fold composition so dish identity, key metadata, and primary action are visible without scrolling.

affordance.interactive-looks-interactive.title: QR code has no affordance signal
affordance.interactive-looks-interactive.description: Screen 1's top-left QR code has no label, border, or container suggesting interactivity. Users may not know it does anything.
affordance.interactive-looks-interactive.suggestion: Is it intentionally unlabeled? If not, add a 'Scan to cook on mobile' caption or button frame.

consistency.same-type-same-treatment.title: Greek Yoghurt card breaks the ingredient grid
consistency.same-type-same-treatment.description: Screen 1's ingredient grid has 13 photo thumbnails and one 'GY' text card on beige. Reads as broken or unfinished.
consistency.same-type-same-treatment.suggestion: Replace 'GY' with a circular thumbnail — photograph or stylized icon — matching the other cards' shape.

consistency.typography-and-spacing.title: Section headers use inconsistent scales
consistency.typography-and-spacing.description: On Screen 2, 'Ingredients' is 24px and 'Cooking Steps' is 28px. Section spacing also varies (16px vs 32px).
consistency.typography-and-spacing.suggestion: Is the difference intentional? If not, unify the header scale and inter-section spacing.

content.evaluation-metadata.title: Recipe has no prep time, servings, or difficulty
content.evaluation-metadata.description: Screen 1 has the photo, ingredients, and steps but no at-a-glance metadata. Users have to estimate fit for time and household.
content.evaluation-metadata.suggestion: Add a metadata row near the title: prep time, cook time, servings, difficulty, dietary tags.

content.trust-signals.title: Recipe shows no ratings, reviews, or attribution
content.trust-signals.description: Screen 1 presents the recipe with no rating, review count, or author byline. No shortcut to evaluate quality.
content.trust-signals.suggestion: Is the absence intentional (curated minimalism)? If not, add rating, review count, and author near the title.

cognitive.density-and-scannability.title: All sections compete equally for attention
cognitive.density-and-scannability.description: Screen 1 has roughly equal visual weight across the photo, ingredient grid, steps, and action bar. No clear starting point.
cognitive.density-and-scannability.suggestion: Lighten secondary content (smaller cards, thinner step numbers) so the eye lands on the dish name and primary action.

mode.current-mode-visible.title: Cooking mode and browse mode look identical
mode.current-mode-visible.description: Screen 1's cook-mode and browse-mode variants look the same except for a button label change. No clear mode signal.
mode.current-mode-visible.suggestion: Add a mode indicator: a 'Cooking' pill in the header, optionally dimming non-essential UI.

layout.element-overlap-integrity.title: Floating bar overlaps the ingredient grid
layout.element-overlap-integrity.description: Screen 1's bottom bar covers part of the ingredient grid — 'Maple Syrup Or Honey' peeks out from under it.
layout.element-overlap-integrity.suggestion: Add bottom padding to the grid equal to the bar's height plus a comfortable margin.

flow.continuity-between-steps.title: Cart-review step appears to be missing
flow.continuity-between-steps.description: Screen 1 shows 'Add to cart' and Screen 3 shows 'Order confirmation'. The cart-review step between them isn't in the flow.
flow.continuity-between-steps.suggestion: Add the cart-review screen — confirm items, enter shipping, pay. Or include it if it already exists.

flow.navigation-back-cancel.title: Users get trapped after step 2 of signup
flow.navigation-back-cancel.description: Signup screens 2 and 3 have no back arrow, cancel link, or close button. The only way out is finishing the flow.
flow.navigation-back-cancel.suggestion: Add a 'Back' link at the top of each step and a 'Cancel signup' option in the secondary nav.

flow.state-preservation-cross-screen.title: Email doesn't appear on confirmation
flow.state-preservation-cross-screen.description: Screen 1 captures the user's email; Screen 3 (confirmation) shows generic 'Thanks for signing up' with no echo.
flow.state-preservation-cross-screen.suggestion: Show what the user just did: 'We've sent a verification link to <email>.'

flow.visual-system-consistency.title: Screen 3 uses a different typographic scale
flow.visual-system-consistency.description: Screens 1 and 2 use 16/24px and rounded buttons. Screen 3 uses 14/20px and squared buttons — visually inconsistent.
flow.visual-system-consistency.suggestion: Is Screen 3 from a different source? If unintentional, unify scale, button style, and spacing across the three.

flow.entry-and-exit-states.title: Onboarding has no entry or exit framing
flow.entry-and-exit-states.description: Screens 1–4 of the onboarding begin and end abruptly. No entry context, no completion state, no clear next step.
flow.entry-and-exit-states.suggestion: Add entry framing ('About 2 minutes') and a completion state ('You're all set — try these next').

flow.progress-indication.title: Multi-step signup has no step counter
flow.progress-indication.description: The four signup screens each show only their own form. No progress bar, step counter, or breadcrumb.
flow.progress-indication.suggestion: Add a step indicator on every screen: '2 of 4 · Profile' or a four-dot progress bar at top.

intent.stated-features-present.title: PRD-stated guest checkout isn't designed
intent.stated-features-present.description: The PRD requires 'guest checkout' for v1, but the uploaded checkout only shows authenticated-user paths.
intent.stated-features-present.suggestion: Add a guest-checkout flow: how the unauthenticated user starts, what info is collected, where it diverges.

intent.design-contradicts-prd.title: Design requires signup despite no-signup promise
intent.design-contradicts-prd.description: PRD states 'no signup required for first audit', but the audit page has a 'Sign up to continue' gate blocking access.
intent.design-contradicts-prd.suggestion: Reconcile: either remove the signup gate or update the PRD if signup is now actually required.

intent.stated-goals-served.title: Signup impedes the PRD's <60s goal
intent.stated-goals-served.description: PRD's goal is 'signup completed in under 60 seconds'. The designed signup is five screens with optional fields shown as required.
intent.stated-goals-served.suggestion: Compress to one or two screens with only essentials. Move secondary fields to a post-signup profile step.

intent.primary-journey-complete.title: Saved Recipes view isn't in the flow
intent.primary-journey-complete.description: PRD's journey is 'discover → save → cook'. Uploaded screens cover Discover and Cook — Save and Saved Recipes are missing.
intent.primary-journey-complete.suggestion: Is Save on a screen not uploaded? If not yet designed, add a Save affordance and a Saved Recipes view.

intent.stated-constraints-respected.title: Mobile breakpoint absent despite mobile-first PRD
intent.stated-constraints-respected.description: PRD states 'mobile-first design', but every uploaded screen is desktop. The constraint isn't demonstrated.
intent.stated-constraints-respected.suggestion: Include mobile variants of key screens. For mobile-first, mobile should arguably be the canonical design.

intent.user-types-served.title: Viewer role isn't represented in the design
intent.user-types-served.description: PRD identifies 'admin' and 'viewer' as distinct roles. Uploaded screens only show admin — viewer variants are missing where permissions matter.
intent.user-types-served.suggestion: Add viewer-role variants for permission-sensitive screens. Show how restricted actions appear (hidden vs. disabled).
